audience: French BTS MAV option metiers du son students (primary); English-language self-learners
isbn_policy: isbn is filled only when seen as text on the publisher's own page; ean13_seen_on_bookseller records the EAN-13 shown on the Librairie Eyrolles catalogue page

resources.title: Le livre des techniques du son - Notions fondamentales
resources.why_recommended: La reference francaise de base pour la theorie du son: acoustique, electricite, psychoacoustique et numerique dans un seul volume. C'est le livre a ouvrir quand un cours de PTES vous echappe.

resources.title: Le livre des techniques du son - Technologies
resources.why_recommended: Le second volume applique la theorie aux equipements (micros, enceintes, consoles, supports, reseaux). Utile pour relier les schemas des sujets d'examen au materiel reel.

resources.title: Techniques de prise de son
resources.why_recommended: Court (208 pages) et concret: choix des micros, couples stereo, console et montage. Bon premier livre pratique pour la premiere annee.

resources.title: Guide pratique de la sonorisation - Concert, spectacle, conference
resources.why_recommended: Guide illustre qui suit l'ordre d'une installation reelle, du choix du materiel au calage des enceintes. Ideal avant un premier stage en sonorisation.

resources.title: Guide pratique du mixage - Sonorisation et enregistrement
resources.why_recommended: Explique la console tranche par tranche (gain, EQ, aux, groupes) avec des exemples live et studio. Tres utile pour comprendre un synoptique.

resources.title: Le guide du MIDI - De l'equipement a l'exploitation : fondamentaux et bonnes pratiques
resources.why_recommended: Couvre la norme MIDI et son usage pour piloter instruments, logiciels et equipements de scene. A garder pour les questions de protocoles et de synchronisation.

resources.title: Pratique des liaisons HF pour la prise de son et la sonorisation
resources.why_recommended: Le seul ouvrage francais dedie aux liaisons HF en tournage et en spectacle. La reglementation des frequences a change depuis 2014: completez avec les sources officielles a jour.

resources.title: L'audio-vision - Son, image et parole au cinema
resources.why_recommended: Texte de reference pour analyser comment le son et l'image se modifient l'un l'autre. Donne le vocabulaire (son in/off/hors-champ, synchrese...) attendu en culture audiovisuelle.
resources.bts_relevance: E2 culture audiovisuelle et artistique, E4

resources.title: Pour une ecriture du son
resources.why_recommended: Reflexion d'un ingenieur du son sur les choix d'ecoute et de mise en scene sonore. A lire en deuxieme annee, quand la technique est acquise.

resources.title: Le son
resources.why_recommended: Introduction accessible a la physique du son, pratique pour revoir les bases de PTES a partir d'un niveau bac.

resources.title: Acoustique
resources.why_recommended: Manuel d'acoustique de niveau superieur, utile pour s'entrainer sur la partie calcul (niveaux, ondes, salles).

resources.title: Initiation a l'acoustique - Cours et exercices
resources.why_recommended: Cours d'acoustique avec exercices, ecrit pour les etudiants des ecoles de cinema et d'audiovisuel. Bon entrainement aux calculs en dB.

resources.title: Prise de son et mixage (Tome 2)
resources.why_recommended: Ouvrage francais de pratique en prise de son et mixage. Signale temporairement indisponible chez le libraire: cherchez-le en bibliotheque.

resources.title: Mastering Audio: The Art and the Science
resources.why_recommended: The standard text on mastering, with clear chapters on metering, loudness and monitoring calibration. Read it after you are comfortable with mixing.
resources.note: Product page shows copyright 2015; Routledge search listing shows 2014.

resources.title: The Mixing Engineer's Handbook
resources.why_recommended: A practical mixing guide built around interviews with working mixers; the 6th edition adds Dolby Atmos, saturation and AI-assisted tools. Easy to read in small chunks.

resources.title: Modern Recording Techniques: A Practical Guide to Modern Music Production
resources.author_or_publisher: David Miles Huber, Emiliano Caballero, Robert Runstein - Routledge
resources.why_recommended: A broad studio textbook used in many audio programmes, covering the whole chain from microphone to delivery.

resources.title: The Sound Reinforcement Handbook, Second Edition
resources.author_or_publisher: Gary Davis, Ralph Jones - Yamaha / Hal Leonard
resources.why_recommended: The classic Yamaha handbook: audio theory explained alongside live-sound practice, from dB and impedance to loudspeaker systems. Still one of the clearest explanations of gain structure.

resources.title: Sound Systems: Design and Optimization: Modern Techniques and Tools for Sound System Design and Alignment
resources.why_recommended: The reference for system engineers on designing and tuning PA systems with measurement. Hard going at first, but it explains why systems are tuned the way they are.

resources.title: Sound and Recording: Applications and Theory
resources.why_recommended: A balanced theory-plus-practice textbook whose scope closely matches the BTS physics and technology syllabus. An older edition was translated into French as "Son et enregistrement" (Eyrolles, 2002).

resources.title: Sound Reproduction: The Acoustics and Psychoacoustics of Loudspeakers, Rooms and Headphones
resources.author_or_publisher: Floyd E. Toole, Sean Olive, Todd Welti - Routledge
resources.why_recommended: Research-based explanation of how loudspeakers, rooms and headphones affect what we hear. Essential for anyone setting up or judging a control room.

resources.title: Handbook for Sound Engineers
resources.author_or_publisher: Glen Ballou, Doug Jones (eds.) - Focal Press / Routledge
resources.why_recommended: A large multi-author reference to consult chapter by chapter rather than read cover to cover. Useful in a school library for specific questions.
resources.note: Routledge search lists 2025; product page shows copyright 2026.

resources.title: Eargle's The Microphone Book: From Mono to Stereo to Surround - A Guide to Microphone Design and Application
resources.why_recommended: The reference book on how microphones work and how to place them, from transducer principles to stereo and surround arrays.

resources.title: Mixing Audio: Concepts, Practices, and Tools
resources.why_recommended: A methodical mixing textbook that explains each processor and why it is used. More structured than interview-based mixing books.

resources.title: The Audio Expert: Everything You Need to Know About Audio
resources.why_recommended: Explains audio fundamentals with a measurement-first, myth-busting attitude. Good for learning to separate facts from marketing.

resources.title: Practical Recording Techniques: The Step-by-Step Approach to Professional Audio Recording
resources.why_recommended: Step-by-step recording guide for beginners, strong on microphone placement per instrument.

resources.title: Sound for Film and Television
resources.why_recommended: Covers sound for picture from the set to the mix stage, by the engineer behind THX. Directly relevant to the audiovisual side of the BTS.

resources.title: The Sound System Design Primer
resources.why_recommended: A gentler entry into sound system design than McCarthy, aimed at students.

resources.title: EBU R 128 - Loudness normalisation and permitted maximum level of audio signals (version 5.0)
resources.why_recommended: The European broadcast loudness rule (-23 LUFS target, true-peak limit). Every sound technician working for TV or radio must know it.

resources.title: EBU Tech 3341 - 'EBU Mode' metering to supplement EBU R 128 loudness normalisation (version 4.0)
resources.why_recommended: Defines how a loudness meter must behave (momentary, short-term, integrated). Read it to understand what your meter displays.

resources.title: EBU Tech 3342 - Loudness range: a measure to supplement EBU R 128 loudness normalisation (version 4)
resources.why_recommended: Defines Loudness Range (LRA), the measure of a programme's dynamics used in broadcast delivery specs.

resources.title: EBU Tech 3343 - Practical guidelines for EBU R 128 (Loudness) (version 4.0)
resources.why_recommended: The practical companion to R 128: how to apply loudness normalisation in production and post. The best first EBU document to read.

resources.title: Recommendation ITU-R BS.1770-5 - Algorithms to measure audio programme loudness and true-peak audio level
resources.why_recommended: The measurement algorithm behind LUFS/LKFS that R 128 relies on. Free download, including a French version.

resources.title: Recommendation ITU-R BS.775-4 - Multichannel stereophonic sound system with and without accompanying picture
resources.why_recommended: Defines the reference 5.1 loudspeaker layout (angles and positions) used in studios and mix rooms. Free download.

resources.title: BTS Metiers de l'audiovisuel, option metiers du son - fiche RNCP37196
resources.author_or_publisher: France competences (certificateur: Ministere de l'Enseignement superieur et de la Recherche)
resources.why_recommended: Official record of the diploma: activities, skills blocks and the decrees (arrete du 4 juin 2013 modifie le 9 mai 2016). Read it to know exactly what the exam expects of you.
resources.note: Record published 09-01-2023; registration valid until 31-08-2027. The eduscol STI pages (referentiel PDF, E3 subjects) could not be reached on 2026-10-22; see not_found_log.

resources.title: INA campus - formations Son (formation professionnelle)
resources.why_recommended: The main French public provider of short professional sound courses (AES67, intercoms, 5.1 mixing, radio). Useful to plan further training after the BTS or via CPF.

resources.title: Pro Tools : prendre en main le logiciel et certification 101
resources.why_recommended: A 5-day (35 h) French-language route to the entry-level Avid Pro Tools 101 certification, the DAW most used in post-production.

resources.title: La Femis - concours, sujets et annales
resources.author_or_publisher: La Femis (Ecole nationale superieure des metiers de l'image et du son)
resources.why_recommended: Past entrance-exam subjects and reports for the national film school, which recruits sound students. Useful for BTS students aiming at a bac+5 after the BTS.

resources.title: CST - Recommandations techniques et mires (son et image)
resources.author_or_publisher: Commission superieure technique de l'image et du son (CST)
resources.why_recommended: The French technicians' association that publishes technical recommendations for cinema and TV, plus free 5.1/7.1 test patterns for screening rooms.
resources.note: Individual sound RT titles not listed in the fetched page.

resources.title: AFSI - Association francaise du son a l'image
resources.why_recommended: French association of film/TV sound professionals: equipment tests, interviews, student theses, pay scales. Good for understanding the profession you are training for.

resources.title: Audiofanzine
resources.why_recommended: The largest French-language audio gear community: reviews, tutorials and forums. Handy for checking what a piece of equipment does before a practical exam.

resources.title: Shure Academy - online training and Pro Audio learning paths
resources.why_recommended: Free, self-paced courses in three levels (Pro Level 1 fundamentals ~4.5 h, Level 2 ~7 h, Level 3 ~14 h) covering sound basics up to wireless coordination. A good free first certificate for a CV.

resources.title: Sennheiser Learn - seminars, recorded webinars and tutorials
resources.why_recommended: Recorded seminars and short microphone tutorials, plus a clear explainer on WMAS broadband wireless, which is changing how HF systems are deployed.
resources.note: Free/paid status not stated on the page; classified freemium conservatively.

resources.title: DPA Mic University
resources.why_recommended: Openly accessible articles on how to mic each instrument and on microphone specs, plus a short pro audio dictionary. Excellent for practical-exam preparation.
resources.note: No price or login shown on the page; classified free on that basis.

resources.title: d&b audiotechnik Education (workshops, seminars, E-Learning Factory, tutorials)
resources.why_recommended: Workshops and seminars such as the Electroacoustics seminar (also run in French in Paris) and online e-learning. Strong on acoustic fundamentals for PA systems.
resources.note: Pricing not stated on fetched pages.

resources.title: L-Acoustics Education - courses and certifications
resources.why_recommended: 20 courses organised by role (System Technician, System Engineer, Immersive, Expert). The French manufacturer's path is the reference for touring PA work in France.
resources.note: Pricing not stated on the courses page; classified paid as courses are booked through All Access.

resources.title: Meyer Sound Education - training courses and tutorials
resources.why_recommended: In-person courses such as System Design & Optimization, plus archived tutorial videos online. Course descriptions alone are a good syllabus for system work.

resources.title: DiGiCo Training - online courses and in-person events
resources.why_recommended: Self-paced online courses on DiGiCo consoles, which are common on large French tours and festivals.
resources.note: Price not stated on the training page.

resources.title: Smaart training (Operator Fundamentals online, labs, certification)
resources.why_recommended: Smaart is the standard measurement tool for tuning PA systems; the free 12-video Operator Fundamentals series is a good start, with paid live classes ($300) and a certification afterwards.

resources.title: The Technology of Music Production
resources.why_recommended: A clear beginner course on how sound, signal flow and processors work in a DAW; also part of Berklee's four-course Music Production Specialization (which includes Pro Tools Basics).
resources.note: Page offers 'Enroll for free' but certificate/full access requires payment; AI-dubbed French available per page.

resources.title: Audio Signal Processing for Music Applications
resources.author_or_publisher: Universitat Pompeu Fabra & Stanford (on Coursera) - Xavier Serra, Julius O. Smith III
resources.why_recommended: Free university course on spectral analysis of sound by two leading DSP researchers. For students who want to understand what plug-ins do under the hood.

resources.title: MIT 21M.380 Music and Technology: Sound Design (Spring 2016)
resources.why_recommended: Free MIT course on recreating everyday sounds by analysis and synthesis in Pure Data; no prior programming needed.

resources.title: MIT 6.003 Signals and Systems (Fall 2011)
resources.why_recommended: The mathematical background of sampling, filtering and frequency response. Optional for BTS, valuable for those going on to engineering studies.

resources.title: Sound On Sound (magazine website: Techniques, Sound Advice)
resources.why_recommended: Long-running UK recording magazine with a large online archive of technique articles and equipment reviews.

resources.title: Sound On Sound - YouTube channel
resources.why_recommended: Video companion to the magazine: technique videos, interviews and show coverage.
resources.note: YouTube page itself not fetched (consent wall); URL taken from the official site.

resources.title: Audio University - YouTube channel
resources.why_recommended: Short, well-illustrated explainers of audio basics (decibels, gain staging, room treatment) suited to first-year students; the site also offers a free ear-training frequency guide.
resources.note: YouTube page itself not fetched (consent wall).

resources.title: L-Acoustics - YouTube webinars
resources.why_recommended: Free recorded webinars from the French PA manufacturer, linked from its education pages.
resources.note: YouTube page itself not fetched (consent wall).
